comments.text: On the subject of medical video games, here's a story you might enjoy: About a decade ago, I self-diagnosed a kidney stone (as close as a layperson can get). The reason is the ancient MS-DOS game "Life or Death" where you play as a doctor who specializes in things like appendectomies. The first step is checking pain locations on the stomach. My pain matched the L-shape from in-game, but since I'd already had an appendectomy, kidney stone was the other option the game covered (which in-game was checked by x-ray).

comments.text:
As a former first responder, the first game was annoying as hell. It didn't follow protocol Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure (ABCDE), then if trauma, Onset, Provocation/Palliation, Quality, Region/Radiation, Severity, and Timing (OPQRST), if medical, Signs and symptoms, Allergies, Medications, Past medical history (Anamnesis), Last meal, Event leading to injury or illness (SAMPLE).

Bleeding should be stopped before loading on a stretcher. As was pointed out, the "seatbelts" and no collar before putting on the stretcher were inaccurate.

Also, multiple ambulances 🚑 should be called on multiple patients emergency.

A paramedic shouldn't intervene in a highway collapse involving chemicals without wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) because they would put their own health at risk. Only firefighters have these PPE available.

Paramedics would locate their temporary hospital upwind, not in the emergency zone.
